purpose: Trofinetide is used to treat Rett syndrome in adults and children 2 years of age and older. Rett syndrome is a rare brain disorder that mostly affects girls and causes problems with movement, communication, and behavior. This medicine helps manage the symptoms of the condition.
how_it_works: Trofinetide is a man-made version of a small piece of a natural protein in the body that supports brain health. It works by helping to reduce inflammation in the brain and supporting the connections between brain cells. Think of it like giving the brain a bit of extra support to help it work a little better and more smoothly.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are diarrhea and vomiting, which can be quite frequent. You or your child may also experience decreased appetite, weight loss, and an upset stomach. These effects often happen early in treatment and may improve over time.
warnings: Diarrhea can be severe and may lead to dehydration, so it is very important to make sure your child is drinking enough fluids. If diarrhea is severe or your child seems very tired, dizzy, or is not urinating, contact your doctor right away. The dose may need to be reduced or stopped temporarily if side effects become too difficult to manage.
typical_dosing: The dose is based on your child's body weight and is given by mouth as a liquid twice a day, in the morning and evening. Your doctor will tell you exactly how much to give. The dose is usually started low and may be increased gradually to help reduce stomach side effects.
